claim: Let \(J>0\) and \(h>0\), set \(k_B=1\), and consider two spin-1 qutrits with Hamiltonian \(H=-J(\mathbf S_1\cdot\mathbf S_2)^2+h(S_{1z}-S_{2z})\). Define \(T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)\) as the supremum of temperatures \(T>0\) for which the Gibbs state \(e^{-H/T}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-H/T})\) has a partial transpose that is not positive semidefinite. As \(h/J\to\infty\), \(T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)=\frac{2h}{\log(4h/J)+o(1)}\); equivalently, \(h/T_{\mathrm{NPT}}(J,h)=\frac12\log(4h/J)+o(1)\). The first loss of positivity is controlled by the partial-transpose block generated by the coherence between \(|1,-1\rangle\) and \(|-1,1\rangle\), rather than the two other off-diagonal blocks.
integrity: The analytic proof uses the exact 3x3 singlet block and the exact partial-transpose block decomposition. Numerical root checks are corroborative, not the proof. A related unindexed derivation remains a residual novelty risk.
scientific_limitations: The asymptotic is restricted to \(J>0\), \(h>0\), \(k_B=1\), and \(h/J\to\infty\). It concerns NPT only; PPT entangled states are not excluded. The finite-field threshold is not solved in closed form.
title: Logarithmic high-field NPT threshold for a staggered pure-biquadratic spin-1 dimer
